title: Tele-Cranio: a CT-free AI solution for remote diagnosis and planning of craniomaxillofacial deformities
zh_title: Tele-Cranio：颅颌面畸形远程 AI 无 CT 诊疗方案
summary: npj Digital Medicine 报道基于手机 2D 面部照片重建 3D 面部与骨性形态的 AI 框架，用于颅颌面畸形远程评估与手术模拟。
key_points: 用手机二维照片重建三维面部与骨性形态
支持基于术者骨性方案的术后模拟
建模数据含539例配对样本、334例患者
reason: 样本量可观、方法新颖，但摘要片段未体现外部验证或前瞻性评估
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is central to craniomaxillofacial (CMF) deformity care, yet dependence on in-hospital imaging constrains remote preoperative assessment and outcome visualization, and repeated imaging can increase radiation and access burdens, particularly for children. We developed Tele-Cranio, a telemedicine-oriented artificial intelligence framework that uses mobile-acquired 2D facial photographs to reconstruct 3D facial morphology, estimate corresponding skeletal morphology and support postoperative facial simulation conditioned on surgeon-defined skeletal plans. Tele-Cranio was developed using 539 paired multimodal samples comprising 2D facial photographs, 3D facial scans and CT-derived skeletal models from individuals aged 3–60 years, including 334 patients with CMF deformities across malocclusion, cleft lip with/without palate, hemifacial microsomia and rare anomalies. Its core model, the Bidirectional Craniomaxillofacial Model-Deformity, learns a shared anatomical representation linking facial soft tissue and skeletal structures across normal and pathological morphology. For remote assessment, Tele-Cranio converts facial photographs into 3D facial surfaces and then infers 3D patient-specific skeletal geometry. For simulation, it generates individualized 3D postoperative facial previews after clinicians complete skeletal planning using standard clinical tools. Validated across heterogeneous CMF subgroups, Tele-Cranio provides an interpretable CT-free layer for remote triage, pre-CT consultation, radiation-free follow-up and surgeon–patient communication, while complementing rather than replacing CT-based definitive diagnosis and operative planning.
zh_abstract: 计算机断层扫描（CT）是颅颌面（CMF）畸形诊疗的核心，但依赖院内成像限制了远程术前评估和结果可视化，而且重复成像可能增加辐射和可及性负担，尤其是对儿童而言。我们开发了 Tele-Cranio，这是一种面向远程医疗的人工智能框架，利用移动设备采集的 2D 面部照片重建 3D 面部形态、估计相应的骨骼形态，并支持以外科医生定义的骨骼方案为条件的术后面部模拟。Tele-Cranio 使用 539 对配对多模态样本开发，这些样本包括来自 3–60 岁个体的 2D 面部照片、3D 面部扫描和 CT 衍生的骨骼模型，其中包含 334 例 CMF 畸形患者，涵盖错颌畸形、伴或不伴腭裂的唇裂、半侧颜面短小症和罕见异常。其核心模型 Bidirectional Craniomaxillofacial Model-Deformity 学习一种共享的解剖表征，将正常和病理形态下的面部软组织与骨骼结构联系起来。对于远程评估，Tele-Cranio 将面部照片转换为 3D 面部表面，然后推断患者特异性的 3D 骨骼几何结构。对于模拟，它在临床医生使用标准临床工具完成骨骼规划后，生成个体化的 3D 术后面部预览。在异质性 CMF 亚组中验证后，Tele-Cranio 为远程分诊、CT 前会诊、无辐射随访和外科医生–患者沟通提供了一个可解释的无 CT 层，同时补充而非替代基于 CT 的确定性诊断和手术规划。

title: Bridging Brain Connectome and Clinical Notes: A Novel Multimodal Framework for MCI Study.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on medical imaging
zh_title: 脑连接组与临床文本对齐的多模态轻度认知障碍框架
summary: IEEE TMI 论文提出将脑连接组与临床报告在共享跨模态隐空间对齐的多模态框架，用于轻度认知障碍研究。
key_points: 以脑子网络为 token 而非原始图像块
在个体与连接组层面跨模态对齐
强调影像与文本关联的可解释性
reason: 方法有新意且已同行评审，但未提及外部验证或临床结局
abstract: [IEEE transactions on medical imaging] Integrating brain imaging data with clinical reports enables the effective use of complementary multimodal information, supporting more accurate and timely diagnosis in real-world clinical settings. This approach has gained growing attention in brain disorder research, yet significant limitations remain: how to encode brain structure and function to reflect meaningful neurological patterns, and how to effectively link objective imaging data with subjective text-based reports while establishing interpretable associations. In this work, we propose a novel multimodal framework that aligns brain connectomes with clinical reports in a shared cross-modal latent space at both subject and connectome levels. Our key innovation lies in treating brain subnetworks as tokens rather than raw image patches, enabling more efficient identification of system-level associations between neuroimaging findings and clinical observations. These cross-modal associations are further fused to enhance mild cognitive impairment (MCI) prediction and provide interpretable diagnostic insights. To our knowledge, this is the first attempt to integrate both structural and functional brain connectivity with non-imaging clinical information. Experimental validation on the ADNI dataset demonstrates performance competitive with recently reported methods. Notably, despite no explicit connectome-token-level supervision, the learned connectome-text associations recover multiple relationships independently reported in the neuroimaging and clinical literature, suggesting that the framework captures clinically coherent cross-modal associations. This pioneering work advances multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) for neurodegenerative disease diagnosis by bridging the gap between neuroimaging analysis and clinical text interpretation through innovative connectome tokenization and cross-modal alignment strategies.
zh_abstract: [IEEE transactions on medical imaging] 将脑影像数据与临床报告相结合，能够有效利用互补的多模态信息，从而支持在真实临床环境中实现更准确、更及时的诊断。这种方法在脑部疾病研究中日益受到关注，但仍存在显著局限：如何编码脑结构与功能以反映有意义的神经学模式，以及如何有效将客观影像数据与主观文本报告联系起来，同时建立可解释的关联。在本工作中，我们提出了一种新的多模态框架，在受试者水平和连接组水平上，将脑连接组与临床报告在共享的跨模态潜空间中对齐。我们的关键创新在于将脑子网络视为 token（标记），而不是原始图像块，从而能够更高效地识别神经影像发现与临床观察之间的系统级关联。这些跨模态关联进一步被融合，以增强轻度认知障碍（MCI）预测并提供可解释的诊断见解。据我们所知，这是首次尝试将结构性和功能性脑连接与非影像临床信息整合起来。在 ADNI 数据集上的实验验证表明，其性能与近期报道的方法具有竞争力。值得注意的是，尽管没有明确的连接组 token 级监督，所学习到的连接组-文本关联恢复了神经影像和临床文献中独立报道的多重关系，这表明该框架捕捉到了临床一致的跨模态关联。这项开创性工作通过创新的连接组 token 化（tokenization）和跨模态对齐策略，弥合了神经影像分析与临床文本解读之间的差距，从而推进了用于神经退行性疾病诊断的多模态人工智能（AI）。

title: AI-ECG Screening for Early Heart Failure Diagnosis
zh_title: AI-ECG 筛查早期心力衰竭：集群随机试验注册
summary: 巴西一项新注册的集群随机试验拟纳入5400人，评估 AI-ECG 机会性筛查能否提高初级保健中未识别左室收缩功能不全的检出。

LVSD is a key finding in the diagnosis of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), a condition for which effective guideline-directed medical therapies are available but which remains underdiagnosed and undertreated. The study will also evaluate the effects of AI-ECG screening on clinical management, healthcare utilization, implementation outcomes, and healthcare costs. The main questions this study aims to answer are: 1. Does adding AI-ECG screening to usual clinical assessment increase the proportion of patients with newly identified LVSD (left ventricular ejection fraction \<50%) within six months compared with clinical assessment alone? 2. Does AI-ECG screening improve the use of echocardiography, the recognition by primary care teams, and the initiation or optimization of guideline-directed medical therapy for HFrEF? 3. How do LVSD detection rates differ between patients identified through AI-ECG screening alone and those identified through clinical suspicion alone? 4. Is this screening strategy feasible, acceptable, and cost-effective when implemented in primary healthcare? Primary healthcare centers will be randomized to either an intervention group, in which AI-ECG screening results will be provided alongside the standard ECG report, or a control group receiving usual care without AI-ECG results. Be referred for echocardiography based on clinical suspicion of LVSD in both groups or, additionally, a positive AI-ECG screening result in the intervention group. 3. Receive educational materials about HFrEF if newly diagnosed, while participating healthcare professionals will receive educational interventions on heart failure diagnosis and management. 4. Complete questionnaires evaluating educational interventions, when applicable. 5. zh_abstract: [新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办者：Antonio Luiz Pinho Ribeiro；疾病/状况：心力衰竭、左心室（LV）收缩功能障碍；类型：干预性（INTERVENTIONAL）；分期：不适用（NA）；入组人数：5400；状态：尚未招募（NOT_YET_RECRUITING）] 这项平行组整群随机临床试验的目标是评估，在巴西公共卫生系统内的初级卫生保健中心接受常规诊疗的年龄≥40岁成人中，使用应用于心电图的人工智能算法（AI-ECG）对左心室收缩功能障碍（LVSD）进行机会性筛查，是否能提高既往未被识别的LVSD检出率。LVSD是射血分数降低的心力衰竭（HFrEF）诊断中的一项关键发现；HFrEF已有有效的指南指导药物治疗，但仍存在诊断不足和治疗不足。该研究还将评估AI-ECG筛查对临床管理、医疗资源利用、实施结局和医疗成本的影响。本研究旨在回答的主要问题是：1. 与单独临床评估相比，将AI-ECG筛查加入常规临床评估，是否能在六个月内提高新识别LVSD（左心室射血分数<50%）患者的比例？ 2. AI-ECG筛查是否改善超声心动图的使用、初级保健团队的识别，以及HFrEF指南指导药物治疗的启动或优化？ 3. 仅通过AI-ECG筛查识别出的患者与仅通过临床怀疑识别出的患者之间，LVSD检出率有何差异？ 4. 在初级卫生保健中实施该筛查策略是否可行、可接受且具有成本效益？初级卫生保健中心将被随机分配到干预组或对照组；干预组在标准心电图报告之外同时提供AI-ECG筛查结果，对照组接受不包含AI-ECG结果的常规诊疗。参与者将：1. 接受常规12导联心电图（ECG），按其初级保健医生的临床指征进行。2. 在两组中，根据临床怀疑LVSD，或另外在干预组中根据AI-ECG筛查阳性结果，转诊接受超声心动图检查。3. 若新诊断HFrEF，则接受关于HFrEF的教育材料；同时，参与的医疗专业人员将接受有关心力衰竭诊断和管理的教育干预。4. 在适用时完成评估教育干预的问卷。5. 接受为期六个月的随访，以评估新识别的LVSD、治疗的启动和优化、医疗资源利用（包括急诊就诊和住院……）

title: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI
zh_title: System 1 智能体：本地可靠快速的工具调用方法
summary: 预印本提出不经文本生成的本地智能体方法，用确定性编译器把工具调用转为选择题，在1952条生物医学工具请求上达97.0%正确率。
key_points: 避免云端大模型暴露患者数据
单次决策模型完成工具选择与参数填充
未出现编造内容，优于18种本地 LLM 配置
reason: 预印本，基准对比充分且关注隐私与幻觉，但未经同行评审、无临床部署验证
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence could automate analyses of sensitive clinical data, but current agents depend on large language models (LLMs). Cloud LLMs expose patient data. Local LLMs hallucinate, and an invented value in a tool call propagates through every later step. Here we present a method to build System 1 agents: local agents that call tools without generating text. A deterministic compiler turns each tool's schema and the request into multiple-choice questions whose options come from the request and the schema, then a one-pass decision model answers them. On 1,952 requests to 157 biomedical tools, the best System 1 agent chose the right tool, or correctly declined, for 97.0% of requests, significantly ahead of all 18 local LLM-agent settings (best 95.2%). The System 1 agent filled 97.0% of 6,056 stated argument values. No System 1 call contained invented content, against 5.5-19.7% of LLM calls. The System 1 Agents framework is freely available as open-source software at https://github.com/eltzanis/SystemOneAgents.
zh_abstract: 代理式人工智能（Agentic artificial intelligence）可自动化分析敏感临床数据，但当前代理依赖大语言模型（LLMs）。云端LLM会暴露患者数据。本地LLM会产生幻觉，并且工具调用中虚构的值会传播到后续每一步。在此，我们提出一种构建System 1代理的方法：这些本地代理在不生成文本的情况下调用工具。一个确定性编译器将每个工具的模式（schema）和请求转换为多项选择题，其选项来自请求和模式，然后由单次决策模型回答这些问题。在针对157个生物医学工具的1,952次请求中，最佳System 1代理在97.0%的请求中选择了正确工具或正确拒绝，显著领先于所有18种本地LLM代理设置（最佳为95.2%）。System 1代理填写了6,056个明确给出的参数值中的97.0%。没有任何System 1调用包含虚构内容，相比之下5.5-19.7%的LLM调用包含虚构内容。System 1 Agents框架作为开源软件可在 https://github.com/eltzanis/SystemOneAgents 免费获取。

title: Auditable Clinical Support with Decision Agents
zh_title: Decision2Care：不生成文本、可审计的临床决策智能体
summary: 预印本提出以决策模型选择电子病历动作的智能体，在546例急诊入院12种疾病上诊断准确率86.5%，并记录每步候选。
key_points: 不输出自由文本，按概率选择EHR动作
546例急诊入院、12种疾病评测
准确率86.5%，对比MIRA-v2的86.1%
中位耗时2.2秒，基线92-100秒
reason: 有基线对照、多病种评测与可审计设计，但为预印本且无外部验证
abstract: Clinicians reviewing a diagnostic work-up will ask what was considered at each step and why the assessment changed. Agents powered by free text can reach physician-level diagnostic accuracy, but their written reasoning does not always reflect the factors that went into the decision. Here, we present Decision2Care, a decision agent that works up the acutely ill patient without producing any text. A decision model assigns a probability to each permitted EHR action, and fixed rules carry out the most probable one. We evaluated Decision2Care on the records of 546 emergency admissions across 12 diseases. Decision2Care reached a diagnostic accuracy of 86.5%, compared with 86.1% for the MIRA-v2 agent, and required a median of 2.2 s per work-up, compared with 92-100 s. Each work-up tracked which options Decision2Care was considering at each step. In 10 of the 12 diseases, the differential diagnosis changed most at the test on which the guideline bases the diagnosis. Where Decision2Care was most confident after a single work-up, all but four of its diagnoses were correct (98.5%). We traced each of these four errors back to a single imaging report. Three of them were corrected when that report was removed. The same kind of decision was used to select the treatments, and Decision2Care's drug orders were judged guideline-adherent more often than MIRA-v2's. In emergency patients, its prediction of death was comparable to that of three intensivists on the same cases. In five of the eight intensive care cohorts, it exceeded the best of the three 24-h severity scores within 2-6 h of records. Our results show that decision agents can carry out clinical work-ups while recording the options, probabilities, and execution rules behind each action for audit.
zh_abstract: 临床医生在审阅诊断检查流程时会询问每一步考虑了哪些可能，以及评估为何发生变化。由自由文本驱动的智能体可以达到医生水平的诊断准确率，但其书面推理并不总能反映决策中考虑的因素。在此，我们提出 Decision2Care，一种决策智能体，可在不生成任何文本的情况下对急性病患者进行诊断检查。一个决策模型为每个允许的电子健康记录（EHR）操作分配概率，固定规则执行概率最高的操作。我们在涵盖 12 种疾病的 546 例急诊入院记录上评估了 Decision2Care。Decision2Care 达到 86.5% 的诊断准确率，而 MIRA-v2 智能体为 86.1%；每次诊断检查所需时间中位数为 2.2 秒，而后者为 92-100 秒。每次诊断检查都追踪了 Decision2Care 在每一步正在考虑哪些选项。在 12 种疾病中的 10 种中，鉴别诊断变化最大的是指南据以作出诊断的检查。在 Decision2Care 单次诊断检查后最有信心的病例中，其诊断除四例外均正确（98.5%）。我们将这四例错误中的每一例都追溯至一份影像报告。当移除该报告后，其中三例得到纠正。同类决策被用于选择治疗，且 Decision2Care 的用药医嘱被判定为符合指南的频率高于 MIRA-v2。在急诊患者中，其对死亡的预测与三位重症监护医师对相同病例的预测相当。在八个重症监护队列中的五个中，其在记录后 2-6 小时内超过了三种 24 小时严重程度评分中的最佳者。我们的结果表明，决策智能体能够执行临床诊断检查，同时记录每项操作背后的选项、概率和执行规则以供审计。

title: No Mastery without the Machine — Medical Education in the Age of Clinical AI
zh_title: 临床AI时代的医学教育：不靠机器难成高手
summary: NEJM AI观点文章认为，AI延伸了临床推理，医学教育应从记忆转向监督与质疑机器推理、识别失效模式。
key_points: AI被视为医学教育威胁，作者认为该担忧合理但不完整
医学历来依赖最佳工具，而非仅靠人类认知
掌握重心转向调度、监督与对智能系统的适度信任

abstract: AbstractAI is often framed as a threat to medical education owing to concerns it may diminish the cognitive struggle through which trainees traditionally develop clinical judgment - a legitimate but incomplete concern. Medicine has never been defined by unaided human cognition; it has been defined by the obligation to use the best available tools in the service of patients. As AI systems increasingly extend not only clinicians' perception, but also their reasoning, medical mastery may shift from memorization and independent synthesis toward the orchestration, supervision, and calibrated deference to intelligent systems. The task for medical education is therefore not to preserve cognitive struggle for its own sake, but to refocus it from recalling facts to interrogating machine reasoning, detecting failure modes, and knowing when human intervention improves care versus when it merely interrupts a better system.
zh_abstract: 人工智能（AI）常被框定为对医学教育的威胁，因为人们担心它可能会削弱受训者传统上借以发展临床判断力的认知挣扎——这一担忧合理但并不全面。医学从来不是由无辅助的人类认知来定义的；它是由为患者服务而使用最佳可用工具的义务来定义的。随着 AI 系统日益不仅扩展临床医生的感知，也扩展其推理能力，医学精通可能会从记忆与独立综合转向对智能系统的编排、监督和有校准的遵从。因此，医学教育的任务不是为认知挣扎本身而保留它，而是将其重心从回忆事实转向质询机器推理、检测失败模式，以及知道何时人类干预能改善照护、何时它只是打断了一个更好的系统。

title: The ITE-Transformer: A pre-trained foundation model for predicting individualized treatment effects from electronic health records
zh_title: ITE-Transformer：从电子病历预测个体化治疗效应的预训练基础模型
summary: 预印本提出基于Transformer的框架，结合纵向病历自监督表征学习与双稳健因果机器学习，预测个体化治疗效应。

abstract: Transformer-based foundation models have shown strong potential for modeling longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), yet existing models focus primarily on risk prediction rather than treatment effect estimation, which limits evidence generation. Here, we introduce the ITE-Transformer, a transformer-based framework that combines self-supervised representation learning from longitudinal patient trajectories with doubly robust causal machine learning for predicting individualized treatment effects (ITEs). As a result, our ITE-Transformer allows to study counterfactual questions of how an individual patient's outcome may differ under alternative treatment strategies. The ITE-Transformer learns temporally contextualized representations of patients' diagnosis and medication histories and subsequently uses these representations to predict treatment assignment, treatment-specific outcome risks, and patient-specific ITEs. The ITE-Transformer is trained using structured EHR data from ~350,000 participants in the All of Us Research Program and evaluated in two clinically different comparative-effectiveness tasks: (i) GLP-1 receptor agonists versus DPP-4 inhibitors among patients with type 2 diabetes, with major adverse cardiovascular events as the outcome, and (ii) immunotherapy versus chemotherapy in a pan-cancer cohort, with all-cause mortality as the outcome. Across both applications, the ITE-Transformer improves the discrimination and calibration of treatment assignment and outcome models compared with existing tabular machine learning approaches and an otherwise identical transformer trained without self-supervised pre-training. The ITE-Transformer further identifies substantial heterogeneity in predicted ITEs and yields interpretable patterns of treatment response associated with patients' diagnoses, medication histories, and comorbidities. Together, our work demonstrates how clinical foundation models can be developed for analyzing heterogeneity in treatment effects and thus support real-world evidence generation.
zh_abstract: 基于Transformer的基础模型已显示出对纵向电子健康记录（EHRs）建模的强大潜力，但现有模型主要关注风险预测而非治疗效应估计，这限制了证据生成。在此，我们介绍ITE-Transformer，这是一个基于Transformer的框架，它将来自纵向患者轨迹的自监督表示学习与双重稳健因果机器学习相结合，用于预测个体化治疗效应（ITEs）。因此，我们的ITE-Transformer能够研究反事实问题，即个体患者在替代治疗策略下的结局可能如何不同。ITE-Transformer学习患者诊断和用药史的时间情境化表示，随后使用这些表示来预测治疗分配、治疗特异性结局风险以及患者特异性ITE。ITE-Transformer使用来自All of Us Research Program中约350,000名参与者的结构化EHR数据进行训练，并在两个临床不同的比较有效性任务中评估：（i）在2型糖尿病患者中比较GLP-1受体激动剂与DPP-4抑制剂，以主要不良心血管事件为结局；（ii）在泛癌队列中比较免疫治疗与化疗，以全因死亡率为结局。在这两个应用中，与现有表格机器学习方法以及一个在其他方面相同但未进行自监督预训练的Transformer相比，ITE-Transformer改善了治疗分配模型和结局模型的区分度与校准度。ITE-Transformer进一步识别出预测ITE中的显著异质性，并产生与患者诊断、用药史和合并症相关的可解释治疗反应模式。总之，我们的工作展示了如何开发临床基础模型来分析治疗效应异质性，从而支持真实世界证据生成。

abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] With the development of artificial intelligence (AI), AI-assisted clinical diagnosis, driven by big data analytics and machine/deep learning (ML/DL), has brought great changes in clinical decision. AI enhances disease detection, classification, and treatment planning by processing diverse data such as electronic health records (EHRs), medical images, and genomics. Key applications include high-accuracy cancer screening, neurological disorder prediction, and diagnostics in ophthalmology, endocrinology, and pediatrics. Significant challenges involve data quality/standardization, model interpretability, and ethical/legal concerns. Mitigation strategies include federated learning, Explainable AI, and fairness constraints. Future directions focus on multimodal data fusion, real-time monitoring via wearables, and collaborative human-AI diagnostics. AI is positioned as a tool to augment clinicians, promising improved diagnostic precision, efficiency, and accessibility in precision medicine, contingent on overcoming technical and ethical hurdles through interdisciplinary collaboration.
zh_abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] 随着人工智能（AI）的发展，由大数据分析以及机器学习/深度学习（ML/DL）驱动的人工智能辅助临床诊断已在临床决策中带来巨大变化。AI通过处理电子健康记录（EHRs）、医学图像和基因组学等多样化数据，增强疾病检测、分类和治疗规划。关键应用包括高准确度的癌症筛查、神经系统疾病预测，以及眼科、内分泌科和儿科中的诊断。重大挑战涉及数据质量/标准化、模型可解释性以及伦理/法律问题。缓解策略包括联邦学习、可解释AI（Explainable AI）和公平性约束。未来方向聚焦于多模态数据融合、通过可穿戴设备进行实时监测，以及人类-AI协作诊断。AI被定位为增强临床医生的工具，有望改善精准医学中的诊断精度、效率和可及性，但其前提是通过跨学科合作克服技术和伦理障碍。
